summary: R. Gordon Wasson was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, later serving in the American Expeditionary Forces, at various newspapers, Guaranty Trust Company, and J.P. Morgan & Co.
R. N. Gadre was an Indologist. In 1959, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.
R. P. Paranjpye studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 1959.

R. Sathyanarayana was an Indologist who completed a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College from 1949 to 1984 and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

R. Thangaswami Sarma worked in Indology and philosophy after studying at Annamalai University and Madras Sanskrit College. He held posts at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

R. Venkatraman works in Indology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, later serving there as Reader, attested in 1990.

Rabindranath Tagore worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School and University College London, and founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.
Philosopher Rachael Wiseman studied at the University of York. Around 2013, she served as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

Rachel H. Pang works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia and was attested in 2019 as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College.

Rachelle M. Scott specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee, attested between 2009 and 2017.

Historian and Indologist Radha Krishna Choudhary studied at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. He held positions at Ganesh Dutt College, Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University, and founded Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Archaeological Museum.
Historian and Indologist Radha Kumud Mukherjee studied at the University of Calcutta (~1901–1905). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, the University of Mysore, and Maharaja's College, Mysore.

Radhika Herzberger works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal and served as Director of the Rishi Valley School from ~1982 to 2012.

Rafal Stepien specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu and Bernard Faure, and held posts at Wadham College and Harvard University.
Rafał Felbur works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a PhD candidate at Stanford University, studying under Paul Harrison, John R. McRae, and Luis O. Gómez.
Indologist and philosopher Raffaele Torella studied under Raniero Gnoli (~1970–1974). He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome from ~1976 to 2020.
Raffaello Orlando specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University in 1981 under the supervision of Denis Twitchett.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and trained under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. He taught at the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad.

Raghu Vira was an Indology, Iranian, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of the Punjab, University of London, and Leiden University, he founded the International Academy of Indian Culture and headed Sanskrit at Sanatan Dharma College.

Indologist and philosopher Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar served as principal of Sir Parashurambhau College. He was also Professor and Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
